title: Measurement Invariance of the Adult Self-Report Across Sex and Ethnoracial Status in the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development Study
titleZh: 青少年大脑认知发展研究中成人自评量表在性别与族裔—种族身份上的测量不变性
abstract: Understanding sex and ethnoracial group differences in psychopathology is critical to identify mental health disparities. However, the validity of these group differences is often uninterrogated. One threat to validity is measurement bias, where specific items may be more likely to be endorsed by a specific group even without differences in underlying psychopathology. We examined measurement bias using invariance testing in the Adult Self-Report (ASR) in adult parents of children in the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) study ( N = 8,608). The ASR dimensions demonstrated invariance across sex and ethnoracial groupings, except for Antagonism and Social Maladjustment. These results suggest that some dimensions of the ASR are largely invariant across sex and ethnoracial groupings in this sample, and that group differences in measured scores are likely unconfounded by measurement bias. We report sex and ethnoracial group differences in psychopathology dimensions and discuss limitations of parental psychopathology assessment in the ABCD study.
summaryZh: ASR各维度在性别与族裔—种族分组上总体表现出不变性，但Antagonism（对抗）与Social Maladjustment（社会适应不良）两个维度例外。 作者据此推断，本样本中ASR多数维度的群体得分差异可能不受测量偏差混淆；该推断限于横断测量不变性证据，不涉及因果效应。 研究报告了精神病理学各维度的性别与族裔—种族群体差异，但摘要未给出具体数值。
